Sub-events.Sub-event_summary: German forces cross the Polish border at dawn

Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_1: On September 1, 1939, at 4:45 AM, German forces launched a massive invasion across the Polish border. The attack came without a formal declaration of war.
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_2: Polish defenses were quickly overwhelmed by the superior German mechanized units and air support. The Luftwaffe achieved air superiority within hours.
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_3: Despite fierce resistance from Polish troops, the German advance continued rapidly toward Warsaw.

Sub-events.Sub-event_summary: Soviet forces enter Poland from the east

Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_4: On September 17, 1939, Soviet forces invaded Poland from the east, implementing the secret protocols of the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact.
Sub-event_fulltext.Paragraph_5: Polish forces, already engaged with German troops in the west, were unable to mount an effective defense against this second invasion.
